title: Introduce entropy-based coverage mapper and compact release atomizer
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: onboarding pipelines produce large sample sets and verbose changelog drafts; reviewers and downstream integrators only need compact, high-information slices. This PR adds two complementary components: (1) an entropy-based coverage mapper that picks a small, representative set of samples that maximizes token-level and latency diversity across an onboarding sample corpus, and (2) a compact release atomizer that packages profile metadata and a tiny sample digest into a single release atom used by release note generators and the registry UI. Design summary: the mapper scores candidate samples with a combined metric (token-entropy + latency-quantile spread + request-path diversity) and then runs a lightweight greedy selection with configurable budget and privacy-aware redaction hooks. The atomizer serializes a profile into a compact protobuf-lite blob plus a human-readable blurb (100-400 chars) and a changelog hint map so downstream changelog automation can assemble targeted release lines without pulling the full dataset. Backwards-compatibility: atoms are additive and stored under the existing profile attachments namespace; existing consumers will ignore the new atom MIME type unless they opt in. Checklist: - [x] Mapper scoring function and unit tests - [x] Atom serializer + compact blurb generator - [x] Privacy redaction plug-in + smoke tests - [x] Integration test for registry upload/download of atoms - [x] Release note generator wiring and example template - [x] Docs (registry API changelog section) Performance considerations: mapper runs as an optional post-onboard job; default budget is 40 samples which keeps CPU and memory well under existing limits in our CI. Linear/Jira: ENG-821 implements the mapper; ENG-987 wires atom output into release drafts; SUP-1432 is support follow-up for a customer onboarding with large corpora. Related: this complements the telemetry-driven sample-sampler work but uses an orthogonal objective (information entropy instead of sampling weights).
commits_summary: 7 commits: initial mapper prototype; add entropy scoring util; integrate latency quantiles; implement redaction hook; atomizer serializer and proto-lite schema; add e2e integration test for upload/download; docs and examples.
review_comments: Marcos Liu: Nice design. Please add a short benchmark to show mapper CPU and wallclock for 10k samples. Also prefer context-based cancellation in the greedy loop.
Asha Patel: Added a micro-benchmark (internal/tests/mapper_bench_test.go) and switched to context-aware loop in commit 4. Benchmarks show ~420ms wallclock for 10k 256-token samples on CI builders.
Sophie Nguyen: Can the blurb generator be localized? We should avoid hard-coded English strings in the atom payload.
Asha Patel: Atom contains an optional 'blurb_locale' and the blurb generator emits a canonical English blurb and a tokenized template; localization hooks added, see docs section.
release_notes: Introduce entropy-based coverage mapper to generate compact, high-information sample slices for onboarding; add compact release atoms to embed profile summary + tiny sample digest for lighter changelog generation and faster reviewer sign-off. Opt-in via profile 'atomize' flag.
notes_for_ops: When enabling the atomize posthook in production, ensure S3 lifecycle policy for atom attachments is set to 1y; atoms are small (~20-60KB) but high-volume onboarding can accumulate.
